diagnosis.what_happened: Previously, when user feedback pointed out wrong results or defective deliverables, the orchestrator performed ad-hoc local patching without triggering the formal learning pipeline to persist lessons across the project.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Treating user corrective feedback as a transient execution glitch rather than a learning trigger causes recurring mistakes, instruction drift, and failure to generalize lessons to subsequent stages.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: Whenever the user provides feedback indicating wrong results, missing elements, or defective artifacts, the orchestrator MUST immediately activate the native learning pipeline (trajectory-analyzer -> behavior-analyst -> knowledge-curator) to catalog the lesson and anti-pattern before/alongside stage remediation.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Continuous self-improvement requires that every negative feedback signal be treated as a durable learning event, ensuring permanent immunity against identical defects in future stages.

desired_behavior: Automatically activate the native learning pipeline upon any user feedback indicating wrong results, defects, or dissatisfaction, persisting structured lessons and anti-patterns.
generalization: Constitutional Zero Silent Patches Invariant: Every user error feedback MUST trigger native learning pipeline execution; ad-hoc patching without durable knowledge curation is prohibited.

evidence.observed_value: The academic-orchestrator should learn to everytime I give a feedback about wrong results or something is wrong, invoke the learning pipeline learn from it.
evidence.threshold_value: 100% learning pipeline invocation on negative feedback
